topic: What interference mitigation techniques are viable for overlapping service transmissions across geographically dispersed ground stations?
consensus_response: The most viable interference mitigation techniques for overlapping service transmissions across geographically dispersed ground stations are rate-splitting multiple access, common message decoding, and machine learning-based techniques. These methods can improve spectral efficiency, reduce interference, and adapt to dynamic environments. Edge computing and NFV can optimize ML-based interference mitigation by decoupling functions from physical hardware, improving resource allocation and real-time performance. However, initial setup costs and virtualized environment management increase, impacting overall system efficiency.

The authors also discuss the challenges of preventing mutual interference between aeronautical communications and terrestrial wireless communications near airports.
